depth_targets.title: SQL execution (Query editor / RDS Data API)
limitations: The data plane is a real engine (sqlite3 by default, PGlite real Postgres on Nano) reached only through the RDS Data API (ExecuteStatement/BatchExecuteStatement) — Vyomi does not expose the Postgres/MySQL wire protocol directly, so an unmodified psycopg2/mysqlclient TCP connection cannot reach it.

BeginTransaction/ExecuteStatement(transactionId)/CommitTransaction/RollbackTransaction are REAL cross-call transactions — a statement that carries the transaction id runs against a connection held open since BeginTransaction and is not committed until CommitTransaction (discarded on Rollback); how many can be open at once is capped by the instance's own max_connections. A statement reading a different connection while a transaction is uncommitted can see a 'database is locked' error on the sqlite engine (Nano's default) instead of Postgres-style MVCC snapshot isolation — a sqlite-specific gap, not present on the PGlite (real Postgres) engine.

depth_targets.title: DB subnet groups
limitations: Subnet IDs and the VPC are stored and returned exactly as given; Vyomi does not validate that they exist in a real VPC (it does not model EC2/VPC in depth for RDS).

depth_targets.title: DB parameter groups and parameters
limitations: Parameters are stored and returned exactly as modified (ModifyDBParameterGroup round-trips through DescribeDBParameters). max_connections is ENFORCED against the RDS Data API's real transactions (rds.data-api) — BeginTransaction on an instance already at its parameter group's max_connections is rejected, not silently accepted; lowering/raising the value genuinely changes that ceiling. Every other parameter (shared_buffers, log_min_duration_statement, innodb_buffer_pool_size, …) remains stored/returned only, with no effect on the underlying SQL engine.

depth_targets.title: RDS Proxy
limitations: Creating, listing and deleting a DB proxy record is real and stateful; Vyomi does not actually proxy connections through it — apps still connect straight to the instance's own endpoint.

depth_targets.title: Option groups
limitations: Option group metadata CRUD is real; adding/removing individual options within a group is not modeled — Vyomi has no engine-specific option catalogue (e.g. Oracle APEX, SQL Server TDE).

depth_targets.title: Automated backups
limitations: The current-region automated backup window is derived from the live instance's retention setting (DescribeDBInstanceAutomatedBackups); cross-region replication of backups and backups retained after instance deletion are not modeled.

depth_targets.title: CloudWatch metrics on the DB instance detail page
limitations: Vyomi does not emit CPUUtilization/DatabaseConnections/IOPS metrics for RDS instances, so the Monitoring tab has nothing real to chart.

depth_targets.title: DB log files
limitations: The sqlite3 / PGlite data plane does not produce real engine log files (error log, slow query log) for Vyomi to list or tail.

depth_targets.title: Read replicas, Multi-AZ failover, connected compute resources, security group rules
limitations: Vyomi does not model a second physical replica, EC2 instances, or VPC security group rule evaluation for RDS; MultiAZ/compute-resource fields are stored and returned but have no runtime effect.

depth_targets.title: Reserved instances (purchase)
limitations: PurchaseReservedDBInstancesOffering records a real, stateful reservation (DescribeReservedDBInstances lists it); Vyomi has no billing system and no reserved-instance-offering catalogue, so the console's purchase wizard (pricing, terms, offering ids) is not built — call the action directly with a reservation id.

depth_targets.title: Capacity reservations
limitations: Capacity reservations are a capacity-market/billing construct Vyomi does not model.

depth_targets.title: Zero-ETL integrations
limitations: CreateIntegration/DeleteIntegration/DescribeIntegrations is real, stateful metadata CRUD; Vyomi does not run the actual cross-service replication pipeline into Redshift, so the console's create wizard (picking a real Redshift target) is not built — call the action directly with source/target ARNs.

depth_targets.title: RDS Custom engine versions
limitations: CreateCustomDBEngineVersion/DeleteCustomDBEngineVersion/DescribeDBEngineVersions registers real, stateful install-media metadata; RDS Custom itself (the customer-managed EC2 instance the engine actually runs on) is out of Vyomi's scope entirely — the console's create wizard is not built.

depth_targets.title: RDS recommendations
limitations: DescribeDBRecommendations derives four real advisories from each instance's own live configuration (no Multi-AZ, an outdated CA certificate, automated backups disabled, deletion protection disabled); Vyomi has no general analysis engine, so it does not generate the full category of recommendations AWS's own monitoring produces (e.g. storage autoscaling, parameter tuning).

depth_targets.title: Exports to Amazon S3
limitations: StartExportTask/CancelExportTask/DescribeExportTasks is real, stateful metadata CRUD that now writes a real manifest object into the named S3 bucket (through the same s3_object_core.put_object every S3 PutObject uses) — a bucket that doesn't exist makes the task genuinely FAIL (Status=FAILED + FailureCause), not silently succeed. Nano has no provisioning lag so a started export completes immediately, and the manifest doesn't carry the snapshot's actual table data — no per-table Parquet dump is produced.

depth_targets.title: Certificate authority rotation
limitations: CACertificateIdentifier is validated on CreateDBInstance/ModifyDBInstance against a real, small CA catalog (DescribeCertificates) — the same identifiers and validity windows AWS publishes (rds-ca-rsa2048-g1, rds-ca-rsa4096-g1, rds-ca-ecc384-g1, the retired rds-ca-2019); an unknown id is rejected (CertificateNotFound), and any instance whose CA differs from the current default is flagged on the certificate-update page with its REAL ValidFrom/ValidTill (no more placeholder dates), with a working 'Apply update now' that really calls ModifyDBInstance. Vyomi does not enforce wall-clock cert expiry at connection time — a cert past its ValidTill doesn't actually block anything.
